Overview

Important Reminder!
Not all setups below will have weapons, characters, or summons that you have, so it's important to test any setups using whatever is available to you. This form of testing is how many Omega setups are created in the first place! Unfortunately, it's unrealistic to list every possible grid permutation and account for every player's inventory.

Seraphic Boost Weapons
As players progress the game, they will be able to replace the weapon that provides a Seraphic Boost with a better weapons. Each upgrade has its own power boosts or activation requirements, so replacing it with a weaker weapon may not yield the same results and could require team or grid adjustments.

Universal Weapons

Weapons that can be used across all elements.

Weapon Rank Copies Notes










Celestial Weapons

Limited Event Weapon

  • Celestial weapons are an incredibly potent grid slot due to their combination of powerful offensive and defensive modifiers. Uniquely, the weapons will provide further bonuses to characters whose weapon proficiencies match the Celestial weapon.
  • Adjust the Celestial weapon type based on your party's proficiencies, or choose one for Voltage II synergy if your party's proficiencies are too spread out.
  • At lvl 200, the weapons can be equipped into the additional slots in Party Set Extra teams and are often one of the more powerful options available.
  • Each weapon can also be awakened, giving it the ability to adapt to whatever the team may need. Since awakening requires Crystallized Core ×170, extra care should be taken when choosing an awakening type.
  • See Advanced Grids#Celestial Weapons for more guidance.










Ultima Weapons
  • Ultima weapons at lvl 200 are a staple in many intermediate to advanced grids due to the versatility of its weapon keys and the various effects they provide.
  • The 1st key affects only characters with proficiencies that match the weapon. Commonly used keys include Gauph Key of Strife and Gauph Key of Strength.
  • The 2nd key grants the entire team with a damage cap increase based on the key selected. This key does NOT stack with a Dark Opus Weapon's 2nd key of the same type, so make sure that they are different.
  • The 3rd key is most impactful since with Gauph Key Tria, the weapon now provides a Seraphic-type attack boost to the entire team, thereby replacing Seraphic Weapons. Depending on the team's needs Gauph Key Tessera and Gauph Key Dio may also be useful.
  • Once you have access to 5★ Destroyer Weapons, Ultima Weapons are not as ubiquitous in team setups due to their stronger Seraphic modifiers and other various effects.
  • See Advanced Grids#Ultima Weapons for more guidance.





World Weapons
  • All World weapons possess a damage amplification modifier, however it is limited to a certain damage type and only available to characters with certain weapon proficiencies.
  • As a result, these weapons are very specific to the composition of the team, not just from a character perspective but also the type of damage the team excels at.
  • World weapons can be equipped in the additional slots in Party Set Extra teams.

Gold Moon Weapons

Warning!

These weapons are very high investment weapons that cost a substantial amount of Gold Moons. They are not recommended to be obtained until the player understands the value of their resources and what benefits they will gain from purchasing one.

Weapon Rank Copies Rating Notes
Hraesvelgr
 High

Hraesvelgr is a unique weapon that allows MC to become a strong damage dealer. Notably, this weapon provides the following:

At all levels, the weapon provides MC with:

  • 4-hit Flurry and 30% amplified normal attack damage.

At Lvl 150, the weapon provides the team with:

  • 100,000 supplemental damage and 10% Damage cap.
  • -100% multiattack rate.

The severe hit to multiattack rate present at lvl 150 has led to a situation where players have created setups for both lvl 149 and lvl 150 Hraesvelgr.

The main differences between Lvl 149 and 150 are as follows:

  • Lvl 150 Hraesvelgr does not need to run Gospel of Water and Sky ×2 in the grid while Lvl 149 will need to.
  • Lvl 150 setups can often struggle to reach 100% TA on MC without clicking extra buttons or without high investment grid/summon options.

As the weapon leans heavily towards shorter rotations, it is usually only seen in faster Full Auto setups and for manual burst rotations and does not see heavy usage in endgame raids.


Shishio
Medium

Typically used as a main weapon for Kengo and Onmyoji. It can be seen as an upgrade to Unsigned Kaneshige. Most notably, it provides:

  • Teamwide C.A. specsC.A. DMG Up (Stackable / Max: 100%)Charge attack DMG is boosted (Stackable / Can't be removed)
    Duration: Indefinite     C.A. DMG Cap Up (Stackable / Max: 50%)Charge attack DMG cap is boosted (Stackable / Can't be removed)
    Duration: Indefinite     at the end of turn.
  • Teamwide charge bar on charge attack and at the end of turn.
  • A large amount of healing on charge attack.

Although the weapon deals 1% of maximum HP to all allies every turn, it is easily counteracted by the sustain provided by the weapon.

Shishio is used most commonly for high difficulty raids and raid solos.

Grid Templates


It's important to adjust your grid depending on the content you wish to tackle. The grids listed below are serve a general guidelines and should be adapted to what you have available.

Many grid templates will reach 280% aura boost as that is a key break point in optimized grids. This is to activate the powerful bonuses granted by Dark Rapture Zero Pendulums (e.g. Pendulum of Extremity) and Anklets (e.g. Anklet of Oblivion). This threshold is easily met in double-sided setupsSetups with Aura Boosts as both main and support summon, however for single-sided setups, extra consideration is needed.

See #Exalto & Aura Boost for further information.

Normal AttacksSkill DamageCharge Attacks

Normal Attack teams tend to be the best burst and Full Auto setups due to their speed. However, compared to Skill or Charge Attack damage, Normal Attacks require more grid investment to reach high damage.

Normal Attack setups leverage the strong synergy between modifiers like Bonus DMG (Echoes), Supplemental Damage, Flurry, and Multistrike.

Due to the limited availability of Odious boosts, setups that use Odious weapons prefer to use their respective Odious summons as both main and support summon. These summons also require copies of Odious weapons in the grid to be fully exorcised to achieve the maximum aura boost percent. Careful consideration is needed when choosing which Befoulments to keep.

Charge Attack setups focus on high damage per turn and often outperform Normal Attack setups in this regard. Additionaly, at a lower grid investment, Charge Attack teams still perform well, unlike Normal Attack setups. However, they are slower in Full Auto due to longer animations and in manual setups, Lockout is a concern.

Charge Attack teams are commonly used in high difficulty raids where consistency matters more than speed.

Building a Burst Setup

Core Concepts

When constructing a normal attack burst team, the folllowing effects should be prioritized:

  • Sources of Bonus DMGDeals bonus DMG for one-foe one-ally attacks
  • Sources of Supplemental DMGDMG dealt is supplemented
     and/or FlurryNormal attacks deal multi-hit DMG to random foes
  • Sources of Instant Attack and/or Double StrikeAttacks twice each turn
    Multistrike
  • Sources of other normal attack related buffs such as Sharp ATK UpATK is sharply boosted
    Assassin (Buff) and DMG AmplifiedDMG for normal attacks and counterattacks is amplified
  • Characters that deal skill damage after normal attacks

With these things in mind, below is a teambuilding example to help you get started!

Character Selection
From some of the characters listed above, we can see that needing triple attack support is a common theme. For this reason, Gabriel will be selected as the first party member as she is a very effective and efficient slot. She provides 20% Bonus DMG and 50% TA, both highly sought after stats in normal attack burst teams.

The other two party member selections are very flexible and any combination of the choices listed above would work well but another thing to consider when choosing a character is what kind of rotation you have in mind.

So who should I put in the missing spot and which setup is best?

You'll have to test it out yourself!
A lot of teambuilding will come down to trial and error and then comparing the results between different setups.
The more you do it, the better you'll get at it!

I want to try create my own setups!

To help create your own setups, below are some curated lists of classes and characters that are useful for normal attack burst teams!

Useful Nightmare Characters

Unite and Fight higher Nightmare difficulty raids often have strong special attacks that give the boss several buffs while also inflicting troublesome debuffs. Building a team that can reliably work around these issues is a large part of the Unite and Fight event experience, so included below is a non-exhaustive list of useful characters players can consider.

Criteria Examples
  • Any characters that provide strong offensive and/or defensive team buffs:
  • Any characters that frequently dispel enemy buffs:
  • Any characters that reliably clear/reduce debuffs:
  • Any characters that frequently provide debuff resistance:
  • Any characters that reliably heal the party:
  • Any characters that provide useful effects as a sub-ally:
